the determination of the structure of membrane proteins, and in particular of bacteriorhodpsin, by electron crystallography.
the development of new techniques for the analysis of electron diffraction images and the application of these to the study of membrane proteins.

the development of new methods for electron crystallographic structure determination and refinement, with the application of these methods to bacteriorhodopsins from Halobacterium halobium and from Natronobacterium pharaonis, and with the analysis of the resulting structural models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of bacteri- orhodopsin is now well established at 3.2 angstrom resolution.
the electron density maps of the protein and the lipid molecules are now sufficiently good to allow the building of an accurate atomic model of the structure of the purple membrane.
the structure of the bacteriorhodopsins has been solved to a level of accuracy that is comparable with that of other proteins determined by X-ray crystallography.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron crystallographic method has now been applied with success to the refinement of the atomic model for a protein with a well-defined structure.
the model of 1BRD is now improved and the accuracy of the co-operative refinement of the protein with its surrounding lipids has been increased.
the structure is now well determined for most of the protein, and the accuracy of the covalent bond lengths and angles are comparable to those in other proteins determined by X-ray crystallography.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron density maps are not as accurate as one would like.

the electron crystallography approach to structure determination can be very powerful, but that the quality of the data and the accuracy of the final structure are limited by the resolution of the diffraction data.
the electron crystallography of membrane proteins is a very powerful technique that is now capable of producing high-resolution structures of membrane proteins.
